title: Reconstruction of the normalized finite smooth-purity tower
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $k$ be a field of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth morphism of pure relative dimension $d$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $n\geq1$ put $A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, let $A_{n,T}$ be its constant sheaf on $T$, and let $A_{n,T}(d)=\mu_{\ell^n,T}^{\otimes_{A_n}d}$ be the $d$-fold roots-of-unity twist [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Form the strict semilinear towers $M_n=A_{n,X}(d)[2d]$ and $L_n=A_{n,Y}$, with transitions the quotient maps (and $u\mapsto u^\ell$ on roots of unity). The canonical reductions $M_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1,X}}A_{n,X}\cong M_n$ and $L_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1,Y}}A_{n,Y}\cong L_n$ satisfy the quotient cocycle. Let $Rf_n^!$ and $\gamma_n=\gamma_{n,A_{n,Y}}:M_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_n^!L_n$ be the finite constructible exceptional inverse image and the finite smooth-purity isomorphisms of [lem-pur-finite-smooth-adjunction-general-base], with its coefficient comparisons $c$ satisfying $c\circ(\gamma_{n+1}\otimes^L A_{n,X})=\gamma_n\circ\lambda$. Then the derived limits $M=R\varprojlim_nM_n$ and $L=R\varprojlim_nL_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] are objects of the completed integral constructible categories of $X$ and $Y$ with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z_\ell$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], their canonical reductions are $M_n$ and $L_n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower, lem-weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower], and under these identifications the $\gamma_n$ identify the finite reductions of $M$ with the tower $(Rf_n^!L_n)_n$ and its coefficient comparisons. Every level is concentrated in degree $-2d$ on $X$ and degree $0$ on $Y$, with constructible cohomology, and the finite levels have compatible etale-origin witnesses.

source.place: Steps 1-3: normalized finite tower, strict reconstruction and identification of finite reductions

proof.text: Use finiteSmoothAdjunctionGeneralBase for the finite smooth system and compactification. Derive relative quasi-compactness and separatedness by composition. Map the nonzero coefficient prime from the base field into global sections to obtain both unit hypotheses.

Apply normalizedTateTensorTower on X at d and on Y at zero, retaining the actual strict towers and projection normalization. Identify the empty finite tensor on Y with the coefficient unit using finiteZeroIso.

For each tower apply singleDegreeUniformReconstruction. Its actual counits give complete constructible limits and canonical quotient squares; combine these with the normalized finite-twist and unit squares supplied by the model theorem. Concentration of the finite models and of the retained levels follows directly from finiteModelIso and the explicit single-complex model via Mathlib t-structure vanishing, rather than an additional hypothesis of the normalized-tower result.

The pro-purity reduction square and naturality at unitReduction give the finite gamma square after finitePuritySourceUnitReduction identifies its source edge. Naturality of scalarComparison pastes this square with both reconstruction counit squares. Invertibility, constructibility and concentration follow from finite smooth purity and the invertible counits, producing IdentifiesExceptional.

theorem condensedTateIntegralTower
    (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ ell)]
    (hchar : 0 < ringChar k)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] :
    ∃ (hfq : QuasiCompact f) (hfs : IsSeparated f) (c : Compactification f)
      (hX : IsNoetherian X) (hY : IsNoetherian Y),
      ReconstructionResult ell f d hfq hfs c hX hY
